text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Monday told Duna TV that the country has lost some of the prestige that it gained at the time of the change of regime, but thanks to the results achieved in the field of stabilisation reforms, it is beginning to regain it.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said he expects to make headway in preparing certain agreements during his upcoming talks with Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin who is due to arrive in Budapest on Thursday. @
- The United Nations High Commissioner's Office for Refugees on Monday awarded its Refugee Prize to the Hungarian Helsinki Commission.
- National Bank of Hungary cut its overnight active repo rates to an annual 27.75 percent from 28.25 on Monday. Also one-week repo rates and passive repo rates have been reduced.

- On December 24, the last metros are scheduled to leave terminals at 4:30 p.m., while buses, trams and trolley buses will leave their terminals at 4 p.m. After 4 p.m. the regular night buses will operate. @
- Two masked gunmen robbed a cash delivery van in downtown Budapest Monday morning and got away with about HUF 70 million cash.
- Heavy snow hit most of Hungary on Monday.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The price of water, sewage system and central heating will also go up by an average of 16-20 percent in several large cities outside the capital in January.
- The new police leadership is planning to establish a special police unit to fight against corruption within all police organisations. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Ministry of Agriculture is gradually taking over export licensing assignments from the Ministry of Industry starting next year, said Minister Frigyes Nagy.
- The average yield on three-month discount T-bill rose again at the latest auction held yesterday.
- Public distribution of the shares of electricity distributor Elmu has been suspended due to suspiciously high subscription volume from the side of primary holders of compensation coupons. @

- At an extraordinary general meeting of Magyar Befektetesi es Fejlesztesi Bank participants made decisions on a HUF 5 billion equity raise, a new business mission, management and personnel issues on Monday.
- Magyar Befektetesi es Fejlesztesi Bank raised Konzumbank Rt's registered capital by HUF 1 billion at Konzumbank's extraordinary general meeting.
NEPSZAVA
- The Budapest Stock Exchange's benchmark BUX index hit another record high yesterday.
Merry Christmas to All Our Readers!
